title: JD Vance talks about the end times and artificial intelligence
seoTitle: JD Vance talks about the end times and artificial.
subtitle: U.S. vice president discussed religious topics and recalled the attack on Donald Trump in interview
excerpt: In an interview with an evangelical podcast, JD Vance discussed the end times, artificial intelligence, and the assassination attempt on Donald Trump.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: The Guardian, Yahoo, The Times of India
contentHtml:
The Vice President of the United States, JD Vance, attracted attention by discussing religious themes, artificial intelligence, and politics in an interview on The Bryce Crawford Podcast. During the conversation with the 22‑year‑old evangelical host, Vance said he would not be shocked if the Antichrist were walking among people and affirmed he is focused on doing God’s work, even if that leads to the end of times. His statements put the American official’s name in the spotlight.

Statements about the end times and the Antichrist

When addressing the Christian prophetic idea of the world’s end, Vance said he does not know whether humanity is already in that period, but he assessed that the final moments will come. According to the vice president, an excessive focus on this subject can be spiritually harmful, emphasizing that his priority is to fulfill his family duties and his role as a leader in the U.S. government.

Vance declared that certain characteristics of today’s world would not surprise him if the Antichrist were present in human interaction. The politician said he tries to maintain an attitude of acceptance, stating that if his actions lead to the end of times or to the building of a better world that prospers long after his death, both outcomes would be acceptable. When asked by the interviewer to rate his certainty of going to Heaven on a scale of one to ten, Vance answered that his assessment falls between seven and eight.

Criticism of artificial intelligence use and spiritual perceptions

During the broadcast, Vance linked his reflections to technology and mentioned artificial intelligence. He cited the case of an acquaintance who uses the tool as a marriage counselor, a practice the politician described as satanic. For Vance, completely removing a person from the social element established by divine creation is highly negative.

The vice president was also asked whether he had ever attended spiritually dark environments. In his response, Vance recounted having participated in meetings with world leaders where certain observations and remarks from other participants gave him a sense of darkness.

Defending Donald Trump’s social‑media post

The interview also covered an AI‑generated image previously posted by Donald Trump, in which the leader was depicted as Jesus. The post made host Bryce Crawford uncomfortable and drew criticism even from Christian supporters before Trump deleted it, initially claiming he had believed the figure showed him as a doctor caring for patients.

Vance defended Trump, arguing that he did not intend to mock or imitate God. According to the vice president, the campaign partner has a sense of humor, enjoys making jokes to keep the atmosphere relaxed, and did not intend to offend the faithful with the illustration.

Remembrance of the 2024 assassination attempt

Vance recalled the attack carried out on July 13, 2024, in Butler, Pennsylvania, when Thomas Matthew Crooks opened fire on Donald Trump, wounding the leader’s ear and killing a supporter before being killed by Secret Service shooters. Vance said that, had the attack succeeded, the United States would have faced a real civil conflict with profound impacts on the legitimacy of the political system.

The vice president admitted that, had Trump’s death materialized, he himself would have shared the suspicion held by many voters that a conspiracy led by shadowy forces had taken the Republican candidate’s life before his return to power. Vance was formally announced as Trump’s running mate on July 15, 2024, completing the ticket that defeated Democrats Kamala Harris and Tim Walz in the November election.

With information from The Guardian, Yahoo, The Times of India.
